title: Leaving a legacy part 1
scripture_text: ‘’My command is this: Love each other as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends. You are my friends if you do what I command. I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know his master’s business. Instead, I have called you friends, for everything that I learned from my Father I have made known to you. You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you so that you might go and bear fruit—fruit that will last—and so that whatever you ask in my name the Father will give you. This is my command: Love each other.’’
devotional:
Every one of us will leave some kind of legacy, we will all cross the finishing line and as we do we will leave behind a memorial to the race we have run and how we ran it.

As we run the race of life it is very easy for anyone of us to fall into the trap of thinking, it’s my life, it’s my race, so how I run it is nobody else business.

We can become small minded and selfish believing the lie that says “Your life is all about you!”

It is easy to forget that every one of us will pass something on to a future generation. It may be something that is wonderful or glorious, or it may be a disappointing legacy of sorrow and shame. The good news is we can choose what kind of legacy we want to leave.

What it says in our passage will help us leave behind a Godly legacy.

If you look carefully at these verses, there is a phrase that Jesus uses that is very helpful when it comes to thinking about leaving a legacy. ‘Remember, I chose you, and put you in the world to bear fruit, fruit that will last.’ Jesus wants our lives to be fruitful.

What does that mean?

The fruit that He is talking about is not what we find in our fruit bowls at home, but it is a changed character, that is, we are different to what we were before we met Jesus. The bible talks about the ‘fruit of the Spirit’ which are all expressions of the personality of Jesus; Love, Joy, Peace, Patience, Kindness, Goodness, Faithfulness Gentleness and Self-Control. When we start bearing fruit these will be evident in our lives. People should see the difference that following Jesus has made in our lives.

How do we bear fruit that will last?

Being fruitful does not mean that you are perfect but it does mean that you are in a process, were you are gradually growing and maturing. For our lives to really count, we need to take our relationship with Jesus seriously. Like the athlete running the race we need to make conscious decisions about what is going get us the best results. As we get closer to Jesus, He will help us to mature into people who really love God. As we grow and begin to produce a Godly character our lives take on a new significance and will make a greater difference for good.

There are lots of things we may not be able to do. I doubt any of us will ever become Olympic gold medallists, but we all have the potential for growth and maturity. If we choose to, we all have the potential to become more like Jesus.
prayer: Father may my life produce a harvest of righteous fruit.
